1	# Creating a command
2	
3	Commands are declared with `defineCommand`, `defineOption` and `defineArgument`, on top of `cliparse`. Options and arguments are validated and parsed by [Zod](https://zod.dev) schemas, and their types flow into the handler. The reasons behind this design are explained in [ADR 0001](../adr/adr-0001-rework-file-structure.md).
4	
5	Before writing a command, look at a similar one and copy its naming, file layout, output format and error messages. `src/commands/drain/` is a good example of a command group with shared arguments and options.
6	
7	## Example
8	
9	A fictional `clever coffee brew <blend>` subcommand, part of a `coffee` group (neither exists in the CLI). The `<blend>` argument is shared by several `coffee` subcommands, so it lives in `coffee.args.js`:
10	
11	```js
12	// src/commands/coffee/coffee.args.js
13	import { z } from 'zod';
14	import { defineArgument } from '../../lib/define-argument.js';
15	
16	export const blendArg = defineArgument({
17	  schema: z.string().regex(/^[a-z0-9-]+$/, 'Use lowercase letters, digits and dashes'),
18	  description: 'Blend of coffee',
19	  placeholder: 'blend',
20	});
21	```
22	
23	`--shots`, `--milk` and `--topping` are only used by this subcommand, so they are defined inline. `--format` comes from `global.options.js`:
24	
25	```js
26	// src/commands/coffee/coffee.brew.command.js
27	import { z } from 'zod';
28	import { brewCoffee } from '../../clever-client/coffee.js';
29	import { defineCommand } from '../../lib/define-command.js';
30	import { defineOption } from '../../lib/define-option.js';
31	import { Logger } from '../../logger.js';
32	import { sendToApi } from '../../models/send-to-api.js';
33	import { humanJsonOutputFormatOption } from '../global.options.js';
34	import { blendArg } from './coffee.args.js';
35	
36	export const coffeeBrewCommand = defineCommand({
37	  description: 'Brew a coffee',
38	  since: null,
39	  options: {
40	    shots: defineOption({
41	      name: 'shots',
42	      schema: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).max(4).default(1),
43	      description: 'Number of espresso shots',
44	      aliases: ['s'],
45	      placeholder: 'shots',
46	    }),
47	    milk: defineOption({
48	      name: 'milk',
49	      schema: z.enum(['none', 'whole', 'oat']).default('none'),
50	      description: 'Kind of milk',
51	      placeholder: 'milk',
52	    }),
53	    toppings: defineOption({
54	      name: 'topping',
55	      schema: z
56	        .union([z.string(), z.array(z.string())])
57	        .transform((value) => (typeof value === 'string' ? [value] : value))
58	        .optional(),
59	      description: 'Topping to add. Multiple --topping can be passed',
60	      placeholder: 'topping',
61	    }),
62	    format: humanJsonOutputFormatOption,
63	  },
64	  args: [blendArg],
65	  async handler(options, blend) {
66	    const { shots, milk, toppings, format } = options;
67

1	# 📖 `clever drain` command reference
2	
3	## ➡️ `clever drain` <kbd>Since 0.9.0</kbd>
4	
5	Manage drains
6	
7	```bash
8	clever drain [options]
9	```
10	
11	### ⚙️ Options
12	
13	|Name|Description|
14	|---|---|
15	|`--addon` `<addon-id>`|Add-on ID or real ID|
16	|`-a`, `--alias` `<alias>`|Short name for the application|
17	|`--app` `<app-id\|app-name>`|Application to manage by its ID (or name, if unambiguous)|
18	|`-F`, `--format` `<format>`|Output format (human, json) (default: human)|
19	
20	## ➡️ `clever drain check` <kbd>Since 4.11.0</kbd>
21	
22	Check that a drain's recipient is reachable and accepts deliveries
23	
24	```bash
25	clever drain check <drain-id> [options]
26	```
27	
28	### 📥 Arguments
29	
30	|Name|Description|
31	|---|---|
32	|`drain-id`|Drain ID|

40	|`--app` `<app-id\|app-name>`|Application to manage by its ID (or name, if unambiguous)|
41	|`-F`, `--format` `<format>`|Output format (human, json) (default: human)|

49	```

51	## ➡️ `clever drain create betterstack` <kbd>Since 4.11.0</kbd>
52	
53	Create a Better Stack drain
54	
55	```bash

57	```

74	
75	### Examples
76	
77	To create a [Better Stack](https://betterstack.com/docs/logs/http-rest-api/) drain, use the ingesting host of your source, along with its source token:

`clever drain` now takes `--type <type>` and only lists the drains of that recipient type. `npm run validate` passes, and `--help` shows the new option. I didn't run `clever drain --type …` against a real app, so the filtering itself hasn't been exercised.

- **Accepted values:** the same names `drain create` uses as subcommands: `betterstack`, `datadog`, `elasticsearch`, `newrelic`, `ovh-tcp`, `raw-http`, `splunk`, `syslog-tcp`, `syslog-udp`. Anything else is rejected with the list of valid values.
- **Filtering:** the API call is unchanged. The handler filters the returned drains by recipient type, so `--format json` is filtered too.
- **Empty result:** the message now names the type, for example `There are no drains of type datadog for <app>`.
- **Where the change is:** the option is defined inline in `src/commands/drain/drain.command.js`, since only the root `drain` command uses it.
- **Docs:** `npm run docs` regenerated `src/commands/drain/drain.docs.md` and `skills/clever-tools/references/full-documentation.md`.
- **Other changes:** I ran `npm ci` because dependencies weren't installed. `fix-all` also reformatted `.claude/settings.json`, so I reverted it.

I haven't committed anything. The project requires an existing issue and `Closes #N` in the PR.
